This lnciim] Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides Sectional ('omm ittee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. Acephate + fcnvalerate emulsifiable concentrate is used as an insecticide in agriculture.

The uiatctial is general Iy manufactured

to contain 25 percent (ndrn) of acephate and 3 percent (m/m) of fenvalerate.

In the preparation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of the [insecticides ,4L/, 1968 nnd tbe Rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under the ACI and Rules, wherever applicable. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2: 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revise@'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

Indian Standard ACEPHATE + FENVALERATE ENKJLSIFIABLE CONCENTRATE -- SPECIFICATION
1 SCOPE This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for acephate + fenvalerate emulsifiable concentrate. 2 REFERENCES "rhe following Indian Standards contain provisions which through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of the standards indicated below: 3.2 Physical The material should requirements specified 3.2.1 Description The material shall be clear, homogeneous, stable liquid, free from sediment and/or suspended matter. It shall readily form an emulsion on dilution with water. 3.2.2 Cold Test No turbidity or separation of solid and/or oily matter or both shall occur when the material is subjected to cold test at 10"C as prescribed in 13.1 of IS 6940 or any other lower temperature purchaser and the supplier. 3.2.3 Flash Point (Abei) When determined by the method prescribed in IS 1448 [P: 20], the minimum flash point of the material shall not be below 24.5 `C 3.2.4 Emulsion Any separation Stabili@ including creaming at the top and as agreed to between the comply with the physical in 3.2.1 to 3.2.4.

The upper limit for conformity shall be the same as those given in 3.3.1.
